newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Hosking quits RNZ's Morning Report for TV - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hosking quits RNZ's Morning Report for TV - paper.

text.p: Mike Hosking has quit National Radio's Morning Report but he'll still be around when Kiwis are having their cornflakes, The Evening Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
Hosking is to host a new breakfast news show on Television One with Susan Wood, the paper said.
Sources said Hosking was head-hunted by TV One director of news and current affairs Shaun Brown and predicted he would move to Auckland to start the new show in August.
The controversial breakfast host has been described as "abrasive", "self-important" and "Mr Rudeness" in letters from irate listeners to The Post.
Hosking, who was not on air this morning, was coy today when approached about his new job. "I can't say anything, I'm sorry," he said.
The broadcaster has a 15-year radio career which saw him shift from commercial talkback to Morning Report in 1994.
But Hosking is no stranger to the small screen. He has been a guest on TV One's Meet The Press and hosts TV3's Sunday, an arts show made by Wellington-based Gibson Group.
TV One has been working on a breakfast news show for some time.
TV2 and TV3 both had short-lived attempts in the early '90s. TV One currently begins its day with BBC news at 6 a.m., Te Karere at 7.45 a.m. and eTV at 8 a.m..
TV2 and TV3 kick off with Home Shopping, Infomercials and cartoons.
